column4:

Policy in the United States From 1970 to 2016
column9:
This study looks at the scope of state policies targeting drug use during pregnancy, how they have evolved, and how they
compare to alcohol use during pregnancy policies.
column14: The number of states with drug use during pregnancy policies has increased from 1 in 1974 to 43 in 2016. Policy started as punitive. By the mid- to late 1980s, supportive policies emerged, and mixed policy environments dominated in the 2000s. Overall, drug/pregnancy policy environments have become less supportive over time. Comparisons of drug laws to alcohol laws show that the policy trajectories started in opposite directions, but by 2016, the results were the same: Punitive policies were more prevalent than supportive policies across states. Moreover, there is a great deal of overlap between drug use during pregnancy policies and alcohol/pregnancy policies.
